name: WeGoLook
summary: On-demand field workers ('Lookers') who go to a vehicle, property or site and capture photos, video and checklist answers in the WeGoLook app. A public order portal sells fixed-price vehicle inspections (auto, heavy equipment, motorcycle, RV, watercraft) from $99; insurers and other enterprises buy custom workflows by contract. WeGoLook is a Crawford & Company subsidiary (Crawford bought 85 percent in January 2017) and also powers Crawford's alternative claims inspections.
short: Sends a local inspector to photograph and video a vehicle or property; online vehicle inspections from $99.

tasks: vehicle inspection ordered online: auto, heavy equipment, motorcycle, RV, watercraft
roof and interior/exterior property inspection (Crawford AIS network)
underwriting and real estate portfolio inspection
notice delivery and product recall checks

pricing.model: fixed price per online inspection; enterprise by quote
pricing.notes: The $99 base and add-on prices could not be re-checked (the portal renders client-side). The public order portal listed Instant Inspection - Auto at a base price of $99, with add-ons: working demonstration and exterior walk-around videos $35, three-day rush delivery $35, two-day rush delivery $50. The same five vehicle products (auto, heavy equipment, motorcycle, RV, watercraft) are listed. Enterprise and claims work (Standard, Self-Service and Custom Looks) has no public price. Looker pay, per the app store listings, is mostly $15-$25 per Look.

latency.typical: About 1.6 days to first inspection on average, against a two-day SLA (2022 claims brochure); rush delivery in two or three days can be bought online
latency.notes: The 2022 brochure also gives 38 minutes average time to first contact and 11.2 miles average Looker distance. The order portal sells three-day and two-day rush delivery as paid add-ons, so standard online delivery is slower than three days, but the standard window is not stated. Crawford says many of its services can be delivered 'as rapidly as same day'. App store listings say most Looks take under an hour on site.

coverage.notes: Over 45,000 Lookers claimed. Crawford describes the Looker network as recruited 'in the U.S.' and lists 'Locations Served: United States' for its WeGoLook contacts; the Looker onboarding site says 'nationwide network'. The homepage and 2022 brochure say 'global' and 'around the globe', but no non-US country is named. A Crawford brochure footer says 'Additional countries served by Crawford's global network'. No city list or density data is public.

licensing.summary: No client terms for deliverables are public: ownership, resale and AI training are not stated. The site Terms (last updated July 1, 2020) say users grant Crawford Inspection Services a license to use their Submissions, and that site content belongs to Crawford Inspection Services or its licensors. The privacy policy (April 27, 2023) says WeGoLook does not sell personal data for money but may share it 'in exchange for other value, such as data analytics'. Enterprise contracts may differ.

human.unknown: Lookers are independent contractors who apply through the app or onboarding site; notary Looks require a notary license and roof inspectors are described as experienced. No identity check, background check or vetting process is described on a provider page. Older partner announcements (2010-2011) describe background-checked Lookers; WeGoLook's current site states no check.

application.unknown: Lookers capture in the WeGoLook mobile app, and release notes describe in-app photo validation and enforced in-app capture for 'v2' Looks, but no app-integrity check, Play Integrity or App Attest use is documented. No C2PA signing; WeGoLook is not on the C2PA Conforming Products List. Capture in the provider's own app or rig is not a server-verified attestation (STANDARD §3).

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: Release notes describe the app's own camera components (front/rear switch, flash, zoom, enforced landscape capture) for photos and video on v2 Looks. Whether gallery uploads are blocked on every Look type, and whether a photo of a screen would be caught, is not stated.

time.method: Reports state an inspection date and time
time.unknown: How the inspection time is recorded (device clock, server receipt or Looker entry) is not stated, and photos carry no visible per-photo timestamp in the sample report.

location.unknown: The app collects precise location and the Terms mention Google geo-location services, but no geofencing or per-photo location check is described. The sample report shows only a city. GPS spoofing risk unknown.

content.method: 'Quality assurance' is listed as a benefit on the homepage; Looks follow a fixed shot list and checklist (see sample report)
content.unknown: No description of what the QA involves, who performs it, or whether every report is reviewed.

corroboration.unknown: No public statement on second-source checks, re-inspections or fraud-rate reporting.

delivery.basis: 2022 brochure: average time to first inspection 1.6 days, two-day SLA; the order portal sells two- and three-day rush delivery.

freshness.typical_age: captured after the order, usually within days
freshness.notes: Each Look is a new on-site capture.

api.notes: No public API documentation. The web order portal (placeorder.wegolook.com) calls a backend at api.wegolook.com with Auth0 login, but it is not documented for third parties. Enterprise integrations are offered as 'Custom Solutions' through sales.

mcp.notes: No entry in the official MCP Registry for 'wegolook' or 'crawford' (2026-10-26).

payment.notes: Online orders are paid at checkout by credit card or PayPal; the order portal redirects to a hosted payment page (Authorize.net or PayPal Express Checkout), per its public config and code (Stripe also appears in that config). Enterprise billing terms are not public.

requester.checks: Ordering online requires signing in or signing up for an account. The Terms require users to be at least 18 and to give accurate registration information.
requester.unknown: No identity, business or purpose checks on who commissions a Look are documented, and the Terms do not address Looks that target a specific person.

Instant Inspection - Auto: up to 64 photos, VIN and damage verification; base price $99; add-ons $35 videos, $35 three-day rush, $50 two-day rush; products for auto, heavy equipment, motorcycle, RV, watercraft; sign-in or sign-up required to order
Order portal config: backend api.wegolook.com, Auth0 login (auth.wegolook.com), PayPal Express Checkout and Authorize.net hosted payment URLs
Sample report: fixed shot list, inspection date and time, city-level location
